transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jane Park (Foresight Head of Search), Carlos Mendes (ML Eng), Rina Patel (Infra), Samir Qureshi (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery focusing on embedding dimensionality and rerank architecture, evaluating hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), throughput targets for product search, and pilot scope (5M vector set, hybrid rerank). Foresight concerned about p95 tail latency (target ~150ms), cost per query, and data residency. Agreed to pilot and exchange pricing/security docs.

Topics: embeddings dims (768 vs 1536), hybrid search vs pure vector fallback, rerank model placement (hosted vs in-house), quantization tradeoffs, dedicated GPU pools, VPC connectivity, SOC 2 and audit logs, benchmark plan (qps, queries per sec, p95), sample dataset specs (5 million SKUs), TTL/caching & prefix cache for product sessions.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alyssa (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intros? we'll try to keep to 45-60, go over your goals and constraints and then surface a pilot path.
[00:00:22] Jane (Foresight): Hi, yeah I'm Jane, I run search. Our main ask is better product discovery on mobile — both precision and speed. We're seeing a lot of query variance, and the current hand-tuned rules are brittle.
[00:00:35] Carlos (Foresight): Carlos here. We handle embeddings in-house currently with an off-the-shelf embedder and Pinecone for storage. We're hitting tail latency spikes during sales spikes.
[00:00:48] Marcus (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say tail spikes, what's p95/p99 numbers?
[00:01:00] Carlos: p95 is around 230ms for single-query search, p99 gets into 500ms in peak. That's with a single vector fanout + shallow post-filtering.
[00:01:12] Priya (Redwood): Are you doing rerank as a second-stage model now?
[00:01:18] Carlos: Yes, a lightweight BERT reranker in the app layer. But it's hosted in our infra; we have to do extra round-trips.
[00:01:30] Samir (PM): And, also cost is creeping — both hosting Pinecone and our GPU infra. We want to explore if Redwood can reduce TCO while keeping p95 under 150ms.
[00:01:45] Alyssa: Perfect — that's the central tradeoff: cost vs latency. We typically evaluate three hosting modes: Hosted API (fast to start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, consistent throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem for data residency). Any must-have from security or residency side?
[00:02:05] Rina (Infra): We need SOC2 Type II, SSO (SAML) integration, and VPC peering options. For some catalogs (regulated partner catalogs) we also need data to remain in our private subnet.
[00:02:18] Marcus: Noted — Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane and VPC peering; we can also run an on-prem package if needed. We'll share the network diagram.
[00:02:33] Jane: Great. On architecture: we want a hybrid approach — vector search first, then lightweight rerank. But we're debating whether to run rerank in Redwood's hosted runtime (low latency if colocated) or keep rerank in our infra to control model weights. Thoughts?
[00:02:50] Marcus: You lose some control if you hand over rerank weights, but Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and can run second-stage ranking as a hosted route. The main consideration is where the KV cache and the short-term session state live — colocating rerank with vector lookup removes extra hop.
[00:03:10] Carlos: One of our blockers is model size — our reranker is ~400M parameters, and we do quantization. If Redwood runs it, we need compatibility with our quantized weights or an API to send logits back.
[00:03:25] Priya: We have tooling for model variants and quantization-friendly execution paths. For binary-incompat issues we can also provide a secure control plane to host your model artifacts in a Private deployment. There's some nuance around how we handle KV cache and continuous batching to hit latency SLOs.
[00:03:45] Jane: Okay. Let's talk scale: our catalog is 5 million SKUs, roughly 10 vectors per SKU on average across variants (so ~50M vectors?). We don't have to index all of them for the pilot, but we want realistic throughput: baseline 500 qps, burst to 2k qps for flash sales.
[00:04:05] Marcus: For 5M vectors that's totally reasonable. Are you storing 1536-dim embeddings or lower?
[00:04:13] Carlos: We're currently using 1536 dims from the public embedder. We experimented with 768 to save cost but saw some recall drop on cold queries.
[00:04:24] Samir: So tradeoffs: 1536 -> better precision, higher storage and CPU/GPU cost. 768 -> cheaper, better throughput, potentially less recall.
[00:04:34] Alyssa: Right. For the pilot we'll pick a representative slice. We recommend convting a blended experiment — compare 768 vs 1536 on the same query set and measure hit rate and conversion delta. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching to reduce token cost for rerank.
[00:04:52] Jane: Does Redwood do automatic prefix/K V caching? Heard something about a KV cache that helps sessions.
[00:05:00] Marcus: Yes, we do automatic KV cache — helps reduce per-token recomputation for chat-like flows and session-level rerank. For product search sessions it can cache intermediate features and speed up rerank, especially when users paginated. Caution: cache locality depends on your session affinity.
[00:05:22] Rina: Network question — if we go Dedicated versus Private, what's the egress model? We need low egress and predictable throughput, not unpredictable bursts.
[00:05:33] Marcus: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; network egress can be optimized with VPC peering and regional placement. Private gives you full control over data egress because it's in your VPC or on-prem. Hosted is easiest but egress costs can be higher without peering.
[00:05:52] Carlos: Okay, about indexing: Do you support sharded vector DBs and fanout limits? Our current setup fans out to 8 shards which helps parallelism but adds tail variance.
[00:06:05] Priya: Yes — Redwood's runtime supports sharded indexes and smart routing. For high QPS we batch and route to multiple worker pools, and we support top-k fanout tuning to cap latency. There's also graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model variant or approximate search during overload windows.
[00:06:25] Jane: How do we evaluate relevance? We want recall@10 and click-through lift. Will Redwood help instrument evals?
[00:06:33] Alyssa: We can ship an eval harness and integrate with your telemetry. Redwood Optimize will give suggestions and regression alerts tied to your prompt/query sets. We'll want your labeled queries for ground truth.
[00:06:45] Samir: Are there examples of customers who've moved rerank into Redwood and seen tail latency improvement?
[00:06:52] Marcus: Yes, a retail customer reduced p95 by ~40ms by colocating rerank and using prefix caching plus a quantized 2nd-stage model. But caveat: depends on model size and sequence length.
[00:07:05] Carlos: On quantization — if we compress reranker to int8, we can save memory but accuracy might drop. Does Redwood support mixed-precision for inference?
[00:07:14] Priya: We do mixed-precision and per-layer kernel selection. We also have recommendations on quantization profiles per workload. Quick note — sometimes embedding vectors can be compressed with product quantization on the vector DB side which reduces storage but affects recall.
[00:07:34] Jane: Important: we have compliance partners that require audit logs for queries. Do you provide per-request audit logs?
[00:07:40] Marcus: Yes — audit logs, token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards. In Private you can ship logs to your SIEM.
[00:07:50] Rina: For the Private deploy, how heavy is the on-prem package? Our infra team wants to know dependencies and whether it needs GPUs on-prem or can run in our cloud account.
[00:07:58] Marcus: The Private package can run in your cloud VPC (we support AWS and GCP). For full-rerank on large models you'll still need GPUs. We can also do a hybrid: vector index in your VPC, rerank runs in Redwood Dedicated with peered connection to reduce egress.
[00:08:20] Jane: Hmm hybrid sounds promising. For the pilot, we want to try Hosted for the embedding + vector lookup and run rerank in our infra to minimize change. But we want Redwood to run a rerank smoke test so we can compare. Is that feasible?
[00:08:33] Alyssa: Totally — common approach. Pilot: Redwood runs embedding + vector DB (we'll point at your index or ingest a copy), and we'll run an optional rerank hosted route for A/B. We'll instrument p95, p99, recall, and cost per query.
[00:08:49] Samir: What about costs for 2k qps bursts? If we go Dedicated, are there burst credits?
[00:08:57] Marcus: Dedicated supports burst capacity options built into the reserved pool, but you can set autoscaling thresholds. Pricing has reserved base + metered burst. We'll include examples in the pricing matrix.
[00:09:12] Carlos: Ok, some nitty-gritty: our queries often have long product contexts (50-100 tokens) and we do some inline filtering. Will token length affect rerank cost badly?
[00:09:23] Priya: Yes, sequence length impacts token cost and latency. For rerank we usually keep input truncated to necessary context or leverage sparse features for filtering before heavy rerank. Also batching small reranks can amortize overhead during high concurrency.
[00:09:42] Jane: Any gotchas for session affinity when caching? We have global traffic across regions.
[00:09:48] Marcus: We recommend region-aware routing. Cache hits are best when affinity is kept for short sessions; for global users you may want per-region caches and a fallback to a slightly higher-latency but lower-cost path.
[00:10:02] Alyssa: Quick checklist for pilot scope: 1) pick sample slice (~500k vectors) representing hot traffic, 2) define qps targets (500 baseline, 2k burst), 3) provide 10-20k labeled queries for eval, 4) decide whether rerank A is in-house or hosted — we'll run both. Agree?
[00:10:20] Jane: Yes. We'll start with 500k and then scale.
[00:10:25] Samir: Can Redwood also help on embedding dimensionality experiments? We'd like automated A/B on 768 vs 1536.
[00:10:32] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize can orchestrate running both index variants and compare metrics. We'll provide sample scripts.
[00:10:40] Carlos: For vector DB integration — we use a homegrown wrapper around Faiss; will Redwood integrate with an existing Faiss cluster or do you prefer to ingest?
[00:10:49] Priya: We support Faiss, Annoy, and managed stores. We can integrate with your cluster over a secure channel, or we can ingest a snapshot into Redwood-managed vector storage for the pilot. Integration tends to be faster if we ingest a snapshot, but production folks sometimes prefer to keep the index in-place.
[00:11:06] Rina: If we ingest snapshot, are there sync primitives for delta updates?
[00:11:11] Marcus: Yes we support incremental updates and upserts. For near-real-time catalogs we'd recommend streaming updates; for batch catalogs, periodic snapshot sync is fine.
[00:11:22] Jane: Any SLA numbers we can expect for Dedicated?
[00:11:27] Alyssa: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets tailored to the reserved pool size; we'll include a sample SLO in the doc bundle.
[00:11:36] Samir: Let's capture open risks: 1) rerank model compatibility & quantization gaps, 2) data residency for some catalogs, 3) tail latency under 2k burst, and 4) instrumentation and deck for business metrics.
[00:11:50] Alyssa: Good call. We'll also run a smoke benchmark to validate p95 under representative workload. Marcus will prepare the benchmark config.
[00:11:59] Marcus: I'll include histograms, p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k requests. Also will include a top-k fanout tuning script.
[00:12:10] Carlos: Our acceptance criteria for pilot: p95 < 150ms at baseline and recall@10 delta <= 1.5% vs current. If Redwood can achieve both with lower TCO, we move to Dedicated.
[00:12:25] Priya: That's reasonable. We'll aim to show a path to that.
[00:12:30] Jane: Curious — do you have an example of cost per 1k queries for 1536 dims vs 768 dims?
[00:12:36] Alyssa: We'll prepare ballpark numbers in the pricing matrix, but expect approx 1.6-2x storage and compute for 1536 vs 768 depending on compression. Quantization/ PQ can narrow that gap.
[00:12:50] Samir: Security & contracts — who owns the logs? Can we request log retention limits?
[00:12:55] Marcus: For Hosted and Dedicated logs are retained per your contract and can be exported. In Private you control retention. We'll include retention options and egress policies in the security doc.
[00:13:10] Rina: On SSO — we need to ensure RBAC maps to our Okta groups.
[00:13:14] Alyssa: We support SAML SSO and RBAC that maps to groups; we'll share the SSO integration guide.
[00:13:22] Samir: Any preliminary timeline for pilot?
[00:13:25] Alyssa: If we get agreement this week we can kick off the week of Apr 2. Marcus will need the sample dataset and queries by Mar 28 to prep.
[00:13:33] Jane: Sounds good.
[00:13:36] Carlos: A couple of small Qs — does Redwood provide versioning for models and rollback?
[00:13:41] Priya: Yes, model versioning and rollout policies (canary, A/B, automatic rollback on regressions). We'll include docs.
[00:13:50] Samir: Ok, wrap-up. Any other major concerns?
[00:13:55] Jane: Just want to make sure we're not forced to change our entire pipeline for the pilot — minimal friction is key.
[00:14:02] Alyssa: Understood. We'll keep pilot non-invasive: snapshot ingest option, hosted rerank smoke test optional.
[00:14:09] Priya: I'll follow up with a short architecture note describing both ingest and in-place integration patterns.
[00:14:15] Marcus: I'll follow up with the benchmark template and the fanout tuning script.
[00:14:20] Alyssa: Great. Next steps recap: Alyssa send pricing and hosting comparison; Marcus send benchmark config; Priya send architecture note; Rina/Carlos share sample dataset and queries. We'll schedule kickoff for Apr 2 week.
[00:14:35] Jane: Thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.
[00:14:38] [Call transitions to post-meeting chatter and screen-share coordination — low-content noise for approx 40 minutes; Fireflies truncated.]

End of transcript.

References/attachments mentioned: pricing matrix (link to be sent), SOC2 + ISO summary (doc), pilot benchmark template (spreadsheet), SSO/SAML integration guide (doc), sample fanout tuning script (gist).
